text: SQL Server Database Administration's escalation and communication lesson covered this for a routine incident. A declared disaster is the same problem at much higher stakes — more people watching, and the team doing the actual recovery shouldn't also be fielding every question as it happens.

The same shape still applies — impact, current action, and an ETA only when it's genuinely known. But at disaster scale, honesty matters even more, because a guessed ETA that turns out wrong, repeated to leadership or customers, damages trust far more than a single missed internal update ever would.

The chain of command needs to be decided in advance, not figured out live under pressure. A dedicated communication role, separate from the recovery team, owns talking to stakeholders. That frees the recovery team to just focus on recovering, instead of splitting attention between the technical work and answering questions.

Every component from DR Plan Components now has real depth behind it — this lesson closes the human side of the plan. Next up: Chapter Nine, the capstone, starting with designing a full HA/DR plan for a real scenario.
